SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. 112C Jmy

S.I, Special Branch Station
REPORT
Date Nov. 19, 1937.

Subject National Salvation Movement in Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Laurier

With reference to Special Branch reports of
November 15 and 17 on the subject of the plan of local
national salvation elements to create disorder in the
Settlement: these elements are now planning to carry out
extensive propaganda in the form of dissemination of printed
matter and pasting of posters in both the International
Settlement and the French Concession on November 20.

On the morning of November 19, a paper poster
(specimen attached) made its appearance on trams running
between Bubbling Well and The Bund. The poster bears
the slogan "Following the withdrawal of the National
troops, we, the people, will continue to resist" and
purports to emanate from the "Mobile Propaganda Group of
the China Labour Circles War Resistance Comrades Association".
It also contains an emblem depicting the chopping of the
sun with an axe.

Subsequent enquiries show that the persons
responsible for posting these slogans on the trams are
members of the 3rd District Water & Electricity Workers'
Union, which has a temporary office at Lane 191, 12 Hart
Road. This union is composed of conductors, motormen and
mechanics of the Shanghai Electric Construction Company.

It is learned that the "China Labour Circles War
Resistance Comrades' Association" (勞動界抗戰同志會)
is the new name of the "China Labour Circles National
Salvation Association", which was formed by members of the
General Labour Union on November 6, 1937, with an office
in the Ling Lih Middle School, Chung Hwa Road, Nantao.
This organization is one of the most powerful national

°. Li Ah-mei (徐阿美), ex-mechanic in the employ of the
French Tramway Company. He was arrested by the French
Police on September 6, 1931, and as a result of a raid
on his residence a large quantity of communistic
literature was seized. On October 20, 1931, he was
sentenced by the 3rd Branch, Kiangsu High Court, to
ten years and six months' imprisonment. It is reported
that he has recently been released.

The "China Labour Circles War Resistance Comrades'
Association" now comprises a membership of about 60 persons,
who have been divided into two sections as mentioned
hereunder :-

1) "Mobile Propaganda Group"

This group consists of about 40 members. The
principal duties of this group are to post posters and
disseminate handbills on the national salvation movement
with a view to keeping before the Shanghai populace the
importance of the war of resistance.

2) "Special Picketing Corps"

This corps consists of about 20 members led by
Loh Tien-tung (陸振棟), husband of Sz Liang, the female
lawyer referred to above. The object of the corps is
to ascertain the military activities of the Japanese
and trace the movements of Chinese traitors.

November 7, 1937. Morning Translation

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers.

LOCAL LABOURERS INAUGURATE NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION.

The inaugural meeting of the Shanghai Labourers'
National Salvation Association took place at 2 p.m. on
November 6 in the office of the Shanghai General Labour Union
in Mei Ka Loong 梅家弄, in the City. Several hundred
persons representing various local organizations, including
the Postal Workers' Union, the Printers' Union, The Motor
Car Chauffeurs' Union, etc., were present.
The meeting resolved that Messrs. Lch Ching-tz, 陸京士
Chu Hsueh-fan 朱學範 and Chow Hsueh-hsiang 周學湘 be elected
as members of the presidium; that 81 representatives from
various labour unions be elected as members of the executive
committee and that the following telegrams be sent out:-
1) That General Chiang Kai-shek and military
officers on the front be comforted.
2) That the Chinese Delegates to the Nine Powers'
Conference at Brussels be urged to demand sanctions against
Japan.
3) That labourers throughout the country be
urged to support the war of resistance.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. .........
Special Branch - S.1. Station,
REPORT
Date November 17, 1937.

Subject. Attempt of local national salvation elements to enlist
unemployed workers and loafers to stage demonstrations.
Made by D.S. Fitts.    Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the contents of the attached report
I have to state that Mr. Sarly, Chief of the Political
Section of the French Police was interviewed this morning
when he stated that similar information had been received
a few days ago by his office. According to the latest
information, stated Mr. Sarly, the staging of the demons-
trations mentioned had been sponsored by the local Chinese
authorities with the object of creating confusion in Shanghai
and jeopardising the Japanese advance in this area. Ins-
tructions, however, were received from Nanking FOUR days
ago to the effect that the scheme was not to be put into
operation. Mr. Sarly is of the opinion that nothing untoward
in the shape of demonstrations will occur in either of the
Concessions. He is having further enquiries made, however,
and should any new developments arise, he will inform the
Special Branch immediately.

Mr. Sarly also intimated that no national salvation
associations of any kind now remain in the French Concession,
all having been closed down by the French Police.

[Signature: D.S. Fitts.]

S.I., Special Branch ... Stalish/
REPORT
Date... November 15, 37.

Subject ... Attempt of local national salvation elements to enlist
unemployed workers and loafers for staging demonstrations.
Made by ... J.J.I. Siu Tse-liang ... Forwarded by ... C. Crawford ...

It is reported that local national salvation elements
are endeavouring to utilize unemployed workers and loafers
for the purpose of creating disturbances and staging
demonstrations in the near future with the following end
in view :-
a) To demonstrate the feeling of the Chinese populace
against the Japanese despite the defeat of the armies.
b) To demonstrate their opposition to the Municipal
Police against suppression of national salvation
organizations.

This movement, it is said, will take the form of
coercing local Chinese shops to declare a strike, and
attacking any shops that ignore this warning. Mass
movements will also be organized with the ultimate object
of repeating the May 30th Incident.

The date for the staging of this movement is said
to be November 20, 1937.

So far no confirmation has been obtained to substantiate
the foregoing report, but enquiries are still proceeding.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.I. Special Branch 664661
REPORT
Date November 17, 1937
Subject Attempt of local national salvation elements to enlist unemployed
workers and loafers for staging demonstrations.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by

With reference to the reported plan of local national
salvation elements to create disorder in the Settlement in the
near future, further information received shows that this plan
has been shelved meantime in consequence of an instruction
received from Nanking persuading the radical elements to refrain
from any activity which may tend to aggravate the international
situation, which the authorities consider quite critical.
Local agitators have agreed to observe this instruction
pending further developments and as far as can be gathered,
they are adopting a wait-and-see policy, but have everything
in readiness for any eventuality.
It is learned that the movement is favoured very much by
those members who harbour radical views and would be successful
with the support of unemployed workers. Among the promoters,
the China Labour Circles National Salvation Association(中國
勞働界抗亡協會 ), is prominent and said to be one of the
most powerful leaders. This organization, which was inaugurated
on November 6, in the office of the General Labour Union, Mei
Ka Loong, City, was formed by local labour circles under the
guidance of Messrs Loh Ching-dz(陸京士), Committee member of
local Tangpu; Chu Hsueh-fan(朱学範), Chairman of the General
Labour Union and Chow Hsueh-hsiang(周学湘), influential member
of the General Labour Union and Chairman of the 4th District
Cigarette Workers' Union, then located on Baikal Road.
Following the withdrawal of Chinese troops from the Shanghai
area, the office of this organization was ostensibly closed.
Although there is reason to believe that private rendez-vous,
such as hotels, lodging houses, and private homes of members,
has been used to maintain its control over local labourers.

It is worthy of note that at the beginning of the local
Sino-Japanese hostilities, Messrs Loh Ching-dz and Chu Hsueh-fan
took an active part in the formation of the Shanghai Special
Service Corps, consisting of labourers. One of its members
was arrested by the Municipal Police on Brenan Road, O.D.L. on
September 10, 1937, and another at the Brenan Road Railway
Barrier on October 24, 1937, both armed with Mauser pistols.
Both Messrs Loh Ching-dz and Chu Hsueh-fan are disciples
of Mr. Tu Yueh-sung(杜月笙), one of the three well known Chinese
in French Concession, who was concerned in the All Shanghai
Association for the Support of Armed Resistance.
Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan is the promoter of the Nyi Zoe Club(毅社)
(unlicenced?), located in Room 510, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue
Edward VII.
